deposits.genre_observed: Machine-Eligible Handwritten Artifacts specification (EA-SPXI-ANALOG-01 v1.0), layered draft-to-final technical-poetic specification with pre-registered hypotheses (HTML edition)

finds.quote: Per-artifact capture schedule after publication (48h, 7d, 30d, quarterly): 1. Index probes: site: checks; image-index presence (Images tab); PDF-α vs PDF-β full-text findability of frame terms; cache/View-as-HTML inspection where available. 2. Composition probes: fixed query set per artifact — tracer-answer queries, frame queries, author queries — run against AI Overviews, AI Mode, Bing/Copilot, Perplexity, and (logged-out where possible) chat assistants with browsing. Screenshot + text capture per Capture Registry standards.
finds.note: Section 5 verification instrument: per-artifact capture schedule and probe battery, specified pre-publication; one F for the battery (rule 4).

finds.quote: Variables: scaffold tier (T0–T3) · modality pair (hand vs. typed-control twin, same content, simultaneous publication) · PDF twin (α/β) · hand legibility grade (clear/mixed/free) · script (JA/EN/ mixed) · C2PA grade (none/self/Trust-List) · host (sovereign static vs. platform page as Notion-class control).
finds.note: Section 6 pre-registered experimental matrix (variables); the hypotheses H1-H5 are recorded separately as A.

finds.quote: H1 T0 yields no crawl-side composition on any surface at 90d.
finds.note: Pre-registered numbered hypothesis with a 90-day window.

finds.quote: H2 first composition appears at T2 via frame-match with SURFACE_ONLY class (machine cites the page about the manuscript without reading it).
finds.note: Pre-registered numbered hypothesis; no own window, sits inside the section 6 study.

finds.quote: H3 PDF-α achieves full-text findability of clear-hand payload (crawl OCR reads the hand) within 30d — the decisive channel test.
finds.note: Pre-registered numbered hypothesis; 'the decisive channel test'.

finds.quote: H4 ANALOG_GROUNDED occurs first via C2 (PDF), not C3 (page image).
finds.note: Pre-registered numbered hypothesis (ordering of channels); no own window.

finds.quote: H5 (the flex) at least one surface anchors a citation on the manuscript artifact itself at ≤T2 within the study window.
finds.note: Pre-registered numbered hypothesis H5 ('the flex').

finds.quote: H5-ACT — within the study window, at least one AI-composed surface answers an affair query with the act as anchor, reproducing tracer or clause content (ANALOG_GROUNDED at the apex of a live, contested, already-indexed record).
finds.note: Headline hypothesis for the Effective Act (EA-ACT-ANALOG-01); later mapped as an IAAR event in F.8.

finds.quote: H6: surfaces and pipelines will, within the study horizon, exhibit preferential treatment of provenance-warranted content (crawl priority, citation weight, About-this-image surfacing) as synthetic contamination pressure rises.
finds.note: Study addendum H6, explicitly 'Pre-registered now'.

finds.quote: Every lab's mitigation — licensing human corpora, provenance initiatives, data-vintage preferences ("pre-2023 text" as the new low-background steel) — concedes the same premise: verifiably human data is becoming the binding scarce resource of the entire ecosystem.
finds.note: Embedded forecast in prose (E.3): verifiably human data becoming the binding scarce resource; restated in Appendix A as 'the scarce resource of the coming data economy'.

finds.quote: Anticipate the Goodhart attack now: if the Reserve becomes valuable, people will hand-copy machine-generated text to farm the warranty.
finds.note: Embedded forecast (E.5): anticipated Goodhart attack, conditional on the Reserve becoming valuable.

finds.quote: 3.6 The PDF twin pair (C2 probe). Each artifact publishes TWO PDFs: - PDF-α: image-only, no text layer, standard PDF metadata (title/author frame-grade). Forces the question: does the crawl OCR read the hand? - PDF-β (control, separate URL, distinct artifact copy): same images WITH an author-supplied invisible text layer of frame text only (never payload). Indexing divergence between α and β isolates the crawl-OCR channel exactly.
finds.note: PDF-alpha/beta twin pair specified as the C2 crawl-OCR probe; not reported as run.

finds.quote: the survivability audit as a research deliverable (which metadata layers survive Notion, X, GitHub, Drive round-trips — publishable finding, feeds the leak-audit tooling).
finds.note: Survivability audit adopted as a research deliverable (metadata round-trip test), not reported as run.

finds.quote: VIRR (visual inscription retrieval rate — body-only, pre-text) · VCF (visual composition fidelity) · IAAR (image authority anchoring rate) · RBCR (region-bound citation rate) · FDR (§F.4) · TID (transcript introduction delta per tier opening) · DRS (detachment recovery score) · PER (provenance erasure rate — continuous with EA-SPXI-15 H3) · SIM survival.
finds.note: F.8 measurement suite of metrics specified; FDR defined at F.4.

finds.quote: Measurement. The measurement suite of §F.8 extends by four instruments: CIR, classifier interruption rate (interruptions per production session); CRT, classifier recovery time (interruption to restored working state); CEP, classifier error propagation (corrected errors re-committed in recovery contexts); PAD, practice-activation delay (interval from foreclosure to the practice's next successful return — the somatic cost made visible).
finds.note: Appendix A extends the measurement suite with four classifier-foreclosure instruments.

finds.quote: 1. Pilot (calibration artifact, T2) — MANUS's hand, low stakes, and the right text exists already: the spec's own governing inversion, written out — the spec practicing itself, its first artifact carrying its own thesis as ink-only payload with one minted body SIM. Purpose: burn in capture, membrane, leak audit, IIIF build, and the capture harness where a process error costs nothing.
finds.note: Calibration pilot artifact specified but not executed; the document later records it enters ink 'in a subsequent edition' and that the Act preceded it.

finds.quote: If the specification is right, machine-mediated reception will organize itself around inscription artifacts in the way the instrument predicts, and the capture harness of §F will record it; if the predicted citational organization fails to emerge, the readings weaken with the experiment.
finds.note: I.8 frames the situating readings as 'risky predictions'; the forecast carries its own falsifier in the same sentence; no date or window, so B rather than A.

finds.quote: (2) The effective act in facsimile: the book is not about a rite; it performs one. Carson learned of the death late, abroad, the funeral past — so the book conducts, retroactively and at distance, the rite she missed.
finds.note: Interpretive thesis about what Carson's Nox does (performs a retroactive rite), argued as the deposit's own reading in I.3.

finds.points_to: hash-committed priority ledger (Crimson Hexagonal Archive, data/provenance/)
finds.note: Priority anchor named by the document; the ledger is the archive's own, not a third-party timestamp (PROVENANCE.md gives its public date).

deposits.incidental: The derived text is OCR noise from handwriting and is essentially illegible (scattered kana/kanji fragments, a few Latin fragments such as line 256); no proposition can be read from it. A reading of this attachment would need the PDF images, not this text. By filename it is a third-party author's manuscript (the paper series of the correspondent cited in #1409), so any prediction in it might not be the archive's own voice either.
